title: CBSE CLASS 11 — English | Sentence Improvement
description: Subject-wise test on Sentence Improvement (English) for CBSE CLASS 11. 50Q.
subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Choose the option that best improves the underlined part of the sentence: The committee has decided to postpone the meeting until next week.

options.text: have decided
options.explanation: The subject-verb agreement is incorrect for a collective noun acting as a single unit.

options.text: is deciding
options.explanation: The verb tense is incorrect; the decision has already been made.

options.text: decides
options.explanation: The verb tense is incorrect; the decision has already been made.

options.text: No improvement needed
options.explanation: The original sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.explanation: Committee is a collective noun. When acting as a single unit (making one decision), it takes a singular verb has decided. The original sentence is grammatically correct.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence:

options.text: She don't like coffee.
options.explanation: The subject-verb agreement is incorrect; it should be doesn't like.

options.text: He goes to school yesterday.
options.explanation: The verb tense is incorrect; it should be went to school yesterday.

options.text: They are playing football now.
options.explanation: The sentence correctly uses the present continuous tense for an action happening now.

options.text: We was happy to see him.
options.explanation: The subject-verb agreement is incorrect; it should be we were happy.

questions.explanation: Option C correctly uses the present continuous tense (are playing) for an action happening now.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Choose the best option to fill in the blank: I prefer tea ______ coffee.

options.text: than
options.explanation: The preposition than is used for comparisons with more or less, not with prefer.

options.text: to
options.explanation: The verb prefer is followed by the preposition to when comparing two things.

options.text: over
options.explanation: The preposition over is not used in this context to compare preferences.

options.text: from
options.explanation: The preposition from is not used in this context to compare preferences.

questions.explanation: The verb prefer is always followed by the preposition to when comparing two things.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Identify the sentence with the correct pronoun usage:

options.text: Him and me went to the market.
options.explanation: The pronouns should be in the nominative case (I and he).

options.text: He and I went to the market.
options.explanation: The pronouns are correctly in the nominative case.

options.text: Him and I went to the market.
options.explanation: The pronouns should be in the nominative case (he and I), and the order is also incorrect.

options.text: He and me went to the market.
options.explanation: The pronouns should be in the nominative case (he and I).

questions.explanation: When pronouns are used as the subject of a sentence, they must be in the nominative case (he, she, I, we, they).
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly demonstrates parallelism?

options.text: She enjoys swimming, to hike, and cycling.
options.explanation: The sentence mixes different grammatical forms (gerunds and infinitives).

options.text: He likes reading books, watching movies, and to listen to music.
options.explanation: The sentence mixes different grammatical forms (gerunds and infinitives).

options.text: The chef instructed us to chop the vegetables, to marinate the chicken, and to bake the cake.
options.explanation: The sentence consistently uses the infinitive form for all items in the list.

options.text: My goals are to travel the world, learning new languages, and experience diverse cultures.
options.explanation: The sentence mixes different grammatical forms (infinitives and gerunds).

questions.explanation: Parallelism requires that items in a list or series have the same grammatical form.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Choose the option that corrects the misplaced modifier in the sentence: Running quickly, the bus was missed by the student.

options.text: The bus was missed by the student, running quickly.
options.explanation: The modifier still does not clearly relate to the subject (the student).

options.text: The student, running quickly, missed the bus.
options.explanation: The modifier correctly modifies the subject (the student).

options.text: Running quickly, the student missed the bus.
options.explanation: The modifier correctly modifies the subject (the student).

options.text: The student missed the bus, running quickly.
options.explanation: The modifier is still misplaced and does not clearly relate to the subject (the student).

questions.explanation: The participial phrase Running quickly should modify the student, not the bus.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: If I had known you were coming, I would have baked a cake. Which option correctly completes the sentence, maintaining the correct conditional structure?

options.text: would bake
options.explanation: The verb tense is incorrect; it should be would have baked for a past hypothetical result.

options.text: will bake
options.explanation: The verb tense is incorrect; it should be would have baked for a past hypothetical result.

options.text: would be baking
options.explanation: The verb tense is incorrect; it should be would have baked for a past hypothetical result.

options.text: No improvement needed
options.explanation: The original sentence correctly uses the past perfect conditional (would have baked) for a past hypothetical result.

questions.explanation: This is a Type 3 conditional sentence (past unreal conditional), which describes a hypothetical situation in the past and its hypothetical result.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Which sentence is most concise and clear?

options.text: In my opinion, I personally think that it is essential.
options.explanation: The sentence is wordy and redundant.

options.text: I think it is essential.
options.explanation: The sentence is concise and clear.

options.text: It is essential, in my personal opinion.
options.explanation: The sentence is less direct than option B.

options.text: Personally, my opinion is that it is essential.
options.explanation: The sentence is wordy and redundant.

questions.explanation: Option B is the most concise and clear. The phrases in my opinion, personally, and I think are redundant when used together.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): The sentence Despite of the bad weather, we went for a walk is grammatically incorrect. Reason (R): The prepositional phrase should be despite the bad weather or in spite of the bad weather.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason correctly explains why the assertion is true by providing the correct usage.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason does explain why the assertion is true by providing the correct alternatives.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is true; it correctly states the alternatives to despite of.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true; despite of is grammatically incorrect.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true; Despite of the bad weather is grammatically incorrect. The reason is also true, as despite does not take of, and in spite of is the correct alternative.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Choose the option that best improves the underlined sentence: Having installed the update, the system became slower and less efficient.

options.text: The system became slower and less efficient, having installed the update.
options.explanation: The sentence still suffers from ambiguity regarding who installed the update.

options.text: When the update was installed, the system became slower and less efficient.
options.explanation: The sentence uses a passive construction that is less direct.

options.text: After installing the update, the system became slower and less efficient.
options.explanation: The sentence still implies the system installed the update, which is incorrect.

options.text: After employees installed the update, the system became slower and less efficient.
options.explanation: The sentence correctly clarifies the subject of the action (employees) who installed the update.

questions.explanation: The original sentence contains a dangling participle (Having installed the update). It incorrectly implies that the system installed the update.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: The committee members have decided to postpone the meeting until next week, due to unforeseen circumstances. Which of the following alternatives is the most grammatically correct?

options.text: has decided to postpone the meeting until next week, due to unforeseen circumstances.
options.explanation: Subject-verb agreement is incorrect for a plural subject.

options.text: have decided to postpone the meeting until next week because of unforeseen circumstances.
options.explanation: Correct use of "because of" and subject-verb agreement.

options.text: have decided to postpone the meeting until next week; due to unforeseen circumstances.
options.explanation: Incorrect use of a semicolon and "due to".

options.text: decided to postpone the meeting until next week, due to unforeseen circumstances.
options.explanation: Incorrect subject-verb agreement and use of "due to".

questions.explanation: The phrase "due to unforeseen circumstances" is grammatically incorrect when used to mean "because of unforeseen circumstances" at the beginning or middle of a sentence to introduce a cause. "Because of" is the correct prepositional phrase to express causality in this context. "Have decided" is correct for a plural subject ("committee members").
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Neither the manager nor the employees was happy with the new policy changes. Which of the following alternatives is the most grammatically correct?

options.text: were happy with the new policy changes.
options.explanation: Correct subject-verb agreement.

options.text: is happy with the new policy changes.
options.explanation: Incorrect subject-verb agreement.

options.text: has been happy with the new policy changes.
options.explanation: Incorrect verb tense and subject-verb agreement.

options.text: was happy with the new policy changes.
options.explanation: Incorrect subject-verb agreement.

questions.explanation: When "neither... nor" connects two subjects, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here, "employees" is plural, so the verb should be "were."
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Having finished his homework, the television was turned on by John. Which of the following alternatives is the most grammatically correct?

options.text: the television was turned on by John.
options.explanation: The sentence still contains a dangling participle.

options.text: John turned on the television.
options.explanation: Corrected dangling participle and clear subject-action relationship.

options.text: turning on the television was done by John.
options.explanation: Passive voice makes the sentence less direct.

options.text: the television had been turned on by John.
options.explanation: Incorrect verb tense and still contains a dangling participle.

questions.explanation: This corrects a dangling participle. The participial phrase "Having finished his homework" must logically modify the subject of the main clause. In the original sentence, "the television" did not finish the homework. "John" is the one who finished the homework and then turned on the television.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: She prefers to read novels than watching movies on a rainy day. Which of the following alternatives is the most grammatically correct?

options.text: to read novels than to watch movies
options.explanation: Incorrect comparison using "than" instead of "to".

options.text: reading novels to watching movies
options.explanation: Correct parallel structure and idiomatic expression.

options.text: to read novels to watching movies
options.explanation: Incorrect parallel structure.

options.text: reading novels than watching movies
options.explanation: Incorrect comparison using "than" instead of "to".

questions.explanation: The verb "prefer" typically takes the structure "prefer (gerund) to (gerund)" or "prefer (noun) to (noun)." "Reading novels to watching movies" maintains parallelism and is the correct idiomatic expression.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: The new software is not only efficient but also it is very user-friendly. Which of the following alternatives is the most grammatically correct?

options.text: but also it is very user-friendly.
options.explanation: Lack of parallel structure.

options.text: but also very user-friendly.
options.explanation: Correct parallel structure.

options.text: but also is very user-friendly.
options.explanation: Incorrect word order.

options.text: and also very user-friendly.
options.explanation: Incorrect use of "and" instead of "but also".

questions.explanation: When using "not only... but also," the elements following each part of the correlative conjunction should be parallel in structure. Since "efficient" is an adjective, the phrase after "but also" should also be an adjective phrase, "very user-friendly," without repeating "it is."
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: He is one of the brightest students who has ever graduated from this university. Which of the following alternatives is the most grammatically correct?

options.text: He is one of the brightest students who have ever graduated from this university.
options.explanation: Correct subject-verb agreement in the relative clause.

options.text: He is one of the brightest students that has ever graduated from this university.
options.explanation: Incorrect subject-verb agreement.

options.text: He is one of the brightest students who ever graduated from this university.
options.explanation: Incorrect verb tense in the relative clause.

options.text: He is one of the brightest students graduating from this university.
options.explanation: Incorrect verb form and tense.

questions.explanation: In sentences like "one of the X who/that...", the relative pronoun (who) refers to the plural noun (students), not "one." Therefore, the verb in the relative clause should agree with "students," which is plural ("have graduated").
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: The manager requested that every employee submits their weekly report by Friday. Which of the following alternatives is the most grammatically correct?

options.text: every employee submits their weekly report by Friday.
options.explanation: Incorrect subject-verb agreement.

options.text: every employee submit his or her weekly report by Friday.
options.explanation: While grammatically correct, it is less concise than option D.

options.text: every employee submitted their weekly report by Friday.
options.explanation: Incorrect verb tense.

options.text: all employees submit their weekly reports by Friday.
options.explanation: Correct subject-verb agreement and pronoun agreement.

questions.explanation: The verb "requested" here implies a subjunctive mood for the clause that follows. Thus, "submit" (base form) is correct for "all employees." Option D also resolves the issue of pronoun agreement with "every employee" by making the subject plural ("all employees") and using the plural possessive pronoun "their" consistently.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Despite being an avid reader, she finds historical novels boring. Which of the following alternatives is the most grammatically correct and clear?

options.text: being an avid reader, she finds historical novels boring.
options.explanation: The sentence still implies an illogical cause-and-effect relationship.

options.text: her being an avid reader, she finds historical novels boring.
options.explanation: The sentence is awkwardly phrased and still implies an incorrect relationship.

options.text: the fact that she is an avid reader, she finds historical novels boring.
options.explanation: Correct introduction of a contrast.

options.text: being an avid reader, historical novels are found boring by her.
options.explanation: The sentence is passive and less direct.

questions.explanation: The original sentence implies that "being an avid reader" is the reason for finding novels boring, which is illogical. The phrase "Despite the fact that" correctly introduces a contrast, stating that even though she is an avid reader, she still finds historical novels boring.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): The sentence "The reason why he failed the exam was because he did not study enough." contains a redundancy. Reason (R): Using "the reason why" and "because" in the same sentence to express cause is grammatically incorrect and repetitive. Which of the following options is correct?

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct identification of redundancy and its explanation.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect assessment of the relationship between A and R.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Incorrect assessment of the assertion and reason.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: Incorrect assessment of the assertion and reason.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true because "The reason why... was because" is a common redundancy. The reason correctly explains this redundancy: both phrases express cause, making one superfluous.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: You are editing an article about the importance of mental health awareness for teenagers. You come across the following sentence written by a student: "It is imperative for young people to understand their mental well-being, and they must also seek help when they are struggling with issues pertaining to their emotional state." Which of the following options best improves the sentence for clarity, conciseness, and impact, while maintaining its original meaning?

options.text: It is imperative for young people to understand their mental well-being; also seeking help when struggling emotionally.
options.explanation: The use of a semicolon does not improve clarity or conciseness significantly.

options.text: Young people must understand their mental well-being and seek help when struggling emotionally.
options.explanation: While clearer, it does not combine the ideas as effectively as option D.

options.text: Understanding mental well-being is imperative for young people, and they should seek help for emotional struggles.
options.explanation: The sentence is still somewhat awkward and less direct than option D.

options.text: For young people, understanding their mental well-being and seeking help for emotional struggles is imperative.
options.explanation: Most concise and impactful, combining the main ideas effectively.

questions.explanation: Option D is the most concise and impactful. It combines the two main ideas (understanding well-being and seeking help) into a single subject phrase, making the sentence more fluid and direct.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: The committee has decided to postpone the meeting until next week due to unforeseen circumstances. Choose the best option to improve the underlined part of the sentence:

options.text: have decided
options.explanation: Incorrect subject-verb agreement

options.text: is deciding
options.explanation: Incorrect verb tense

options.text: decides
options.explanation: Incorrect subject-verb agreement

options.text: no improvement needed
options.explanation: The original sentence is grammatically correct

questions.explanation: Committee can be treated as a singular noun when acting as a single unit, which it is in this context (deciding unanimously). Hence, 'has decided' is grammatically correct.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: While waiting for the bus, a sudden downpour drenched him completely. Choose the best option to improve the underlined part of the sentence:

options.text: he was drenched completely by a sudden downpour
options.explanation: Changes the sentence structure but doesn't address the dangling modifier

options.text: a sudden downpour completely drenched him
options.explanation: Does not address the dangling modifier

options.text: he was completely drenched by a sudden downpour
options.explanation: Correctly places 'he' as the subject, addressing the dangling modifier

options.text: a sudden downpour completely drenched upon him
options.explanation: Incorrect preposition usage

questions.explanation: The original sentence suffers from a dangling modifier. 'While waiting for the bus' implies that the subject of the main clause was doing the waiting. Option C correctly places 'he' as the subject, ensuring logical coherence.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: She not only excels in academics but also in sports. Choose the best option to improve the underlined part of the sentence:

options.text: but also excels in sports
options.explanation: Breaks the parallelism

options.text: but also in sports
options.explanation: Lacks a verb for parallelism

options.text: but also excelling in sports
options.explanation: Changes the verb form, breaking parallelism

options.text: but also for sports
options.explanation: Incorrect preposition usage

questions.explanation: The structure 'not only... but also...' requires parallelism. Since 'in academics' uses a prepositional phrase, the second part should also use a prepositional phrase ('in sports'). The original sentence already achieves this parallelism correctly.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Despite his efforts, the company’s profits declined a lot. Choose the best option to improve the underlined part of the sentence:

options.text: declined in a great amount
options.explanation: Wordy and less formal

options.text: declined greatly
options.explanation: Less precise than 'significantly'

options.text: declined significantly
options.explanation: More formal and precise

options.text: declined too much
options.explanation: Informal and less precise

questions.explanation: 'Declined a lot' is informal. 'Declined significantly' is a more formal and precise way to express a considerable decrease, making it the most appropriate improvement for formal writing.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: The new policy will effect positive changes in the community. Choose the best option to improve the underlined part of the sentence:

options.text: affect
options.explanation: Incorrect verb choice

options.text: effect
options.explanation: Correct verb choice

options.text: effecting
options.explanation: Incorrect verb form

options.text: affects
options.explanation: Incorrect verb form and choice

questions.explanation: 'Effect' as a verb means 'to bring about' or 'to cause to happen,' which fits the context of the new policy bringing about changes. 'Affect' as a verb means 'to influence.' Therefore, 'effect' is correct here.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Had I known about the party, I would have attended it. Choose the best option to improve the underlined part of the sentence:

options.text: I will attend it
options.explanation: Incorrect verb tense

options.text: I would attend it
options.explanation: Incorrect conditional structure

options.text: I had attended it
options.explanation: Incorrect verb tense and conditional structure

options.text: no improvement needed
options.explanation: The original sentence is grammatically correct

questions.explanation: This is a correct third conditional sentence structure (past perfect in the 'if' clause, 'would have + past participle' in the main clause), often inverted as 'Had I known...'. The original sentence is grammatically sound.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): The sentence 'Being a rainy day, we decided to stay indoors' is grammatically incorrect. Reason (R): The participial phrase 'Being a rainy day' lacks a proper subject and therefore dangles. Choose the correct option:

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason R is incorrect

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason R is incorrect

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Assertion A is true, but Reason R incorrectly explains why the sentence is grammatically incorrect

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Assertion A is true, and Reason R is incorrect

questions.explanation: Assertion A is true; the sentence is grammatically incorrect due to a dangling modifier. However, Reason R is false. While the phrase 'Being a rainy day' does lack a subject, it's not that it 'lacks a proper subject and therefore dangles.' The correct way to fix this is to provide a subject for the participial phrase, e.g., 'Since it was a rainy day...' or 'It being a rainy day...'.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: A local newspaper report stated: 'The city council held a meeting yesterday. During the discussions, it was decided by them to implement new recycling bins. This initiative aims to reduce landfill waste by 15%.' Which option best improves the underlined sentence in the report?

options.text: It was decided by the council to implement new recycling bins.
options.explanation: Still uses passive voice

options.text: They decided to implement new recycling bins.
options.explanation: Lacks clarity on who 'they' refers to

options.text: The council decided to implement new recycling bins.
options.explanation: Uses active voice and clearly states the subject

options.text: New recycling bins were decided to be implemented by them.
options.explanation: Wordy and still uses vague pronoun reference

questions.explanation: The original sentence uses passive voice ('it was decided by them') and vague pronoun reference ('them'). Option C uses active voice and clearly states the subject ('The council'), making the sentence more concise, direct, and formal, which is appropriate for a newspaper report.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Among the two candidates, John is the most experienced. Choose the best option to improve the underlined part of the sentence:

options.text: most experienced
options.explanation: Incorrect degree of comparison

options.text: the more experienced
options.explanation: Correct degree of comparison for comparing two items

options.text: the much experienced
options.explanation: Incorrect degree of comparison and word choice

options.text: more experienced
options.explanation: Lacks the definite article 'the' for clarity

questions.explanation: When comparing exactly two items or people, the comparative degree is used, not the superlative. Therefore, 'the more experienced' is correct.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: The manager asked the team members to submit their reports by Friday, which was a strict deadline that could not be extended. Choose the best option to improve the underlined part of the sentence:

options.text: by Friday, a strict deadline that could not be extended.
options.explanation: Still wordy and less formal

options.text: by Friday, which was a strict, non-extendable deadline.
options.explanation: Still uses the wordy 'which was' construction

options.text: by Friday, a strict, non-extendable deadline.
options.explanation: Concise, elegant, and clearly conveys the deadline's nature

options.text: by Friday; this deadline was strict and could not be extended.
options.explanation: Less formal and still wordy

questions.explanation: The original sentence is wordy and somewhat repetitive with 'which was... that could not be extended.' Option C is the most concise and elegant improvement. It uses an appositive phrase ('a strict, non-extendable deadline') to effectively convey all the necessary information in a streamlined manner, eliminating redundant words and improving flow.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is correctly improved for clarity and conciseness?

options.text: The reason why he failed is because he didn’t study.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because it uses redundant language.

options.text: He failed due to not studying.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because it is not as clear and concise as Option C.

options.text: He failed because he didn’t study.
options.explanation: This option is correct as it avoids redundancy and is grammatically precise.

options.text: The cause of his failure was because he didn’t study.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because it uses redundant language.

questions.explanation: Option C is correct as it avoids redundancy and is grammatically precise.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is the most improved version of 'The teacher gave the student a book and a pen to write the exam'?

options.text: The teacher gave a book and a pen to the student for writing the exam
options.explanation: This sentence is grammatically correct but less clear about the purpose.

options.text: The teacher gave the student a book and a pen for the exam
options.explanation: This sentence is concise but does not explicitly state the purpose.

options.text: The teacher gave the student a book and a pen so that he could write the exam
options.explanation: This sentence clearly states the purpose of giving the book and pen.

options.text: The teacher gave the student a book and a pen to write his exam
options.explanation: This sentence is grammatically correct but less formal and clear than option C.

questions.explanation: Option C clearly states the purpose of giving the book and pen, which is to enable the student to write the exam.
questions.hint: Look for the sentence that explicitly mentions the purpose of the action.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is in the passive voice?

options.text: The dog bites the man
options.explanation: This sentence is in the active voice, where the subject 'the dog' performs the action.

options.text: The man was bitten by the dog
options.explanation: This sentence is in the passive voice, where the subject 'the man' receives the action.

options.text: The man is bitten by the dog every day
options.explanation: This sentence is in the passive voice but is not the best example as it uses a present tense.

options.text: The dog is biting the man
options.explanation: This sentence is in the active voice, where the subject 'the dog' performs the action.

questions.explanation: The passive voice is used when the subject receives the action of the verb. In option B, 'the man' is the subject receiving the action 'was bitten'.
questions.hint: Passive voice sentences often use the verb 'to be' followed by the past participle of the main verb.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is the most improved version of 'By the time I reached the station, the train had already left'?

options.text: When I reached the station, the train had already left
options.explanation: This sentence changes the structure but does not improve the original sentence.

options.text: By the time I reached the station, the train left
options.explanation: This sentence incorrectly changes the tense of 'left'.

options.text: By the time I reached the station, the train had already departed
options.explanation: This sentence uses a more formal word 'departed' and maintains the correct tense.

options.text: When I reached the station, the train had left
options.explanation: This sentence changes the structure but does not improve the original sentence.

questions.explanation: Option C uses the more formal word 'departed' and maintains the same meaning as the original sentence.
questions.hint: Look for a sentence that uses a more formal synonym for 'left' while keeping the meaning intact.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Which of the following is a suitable assertion and reason for the sentence 'The new policy has been implemented to reduce traffic congestion'?

options.text: Assertion: The new policy aims to reduce traffic congestion. Reason: It has been implemented recently
options.explanation: The assertion and reason are reversed in this option.

options.text: Assertion: The new policy has been implemented. Reason: It aims to reduce traffic congestion
options.explanation: This option correctly pairs the assertion with the reason.

options.text: Assertion: Traffic congestion is a major problem. Reason: The new policy has been implemented
options.explanation: The assertion does not match the original sentence.

options.text: Assertion: The new policy is effective. Reason: It reduces traffic congestion
options.explanation: The assertion assumes effectiveness, which is not stated in the original sentence.

questions.explanation: Option B correctly states the assertion as the fact that the policy has been implemented and the reason as its purpose.
questions.hint: Look for an option where the assertion is a fact and the reason explains the purpose behind it.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is the most improved version of 'If I will study hard, I will pass the exam'?

options.text: If I study hard, I will pass the exam
options.explanation: This sentence uses the correct conditional tense.
